content.text: This matches the preferred position on every material term.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: The renewal regime meets the preferred position in full. § 8.2 provides automatic twelve-month (not multi-year) renewal terms that Customer may exit on only thirty days' written notice, with a Vendor reminder due sixty days before renewal and an extension of Customer's opt-out deadline if the reminder is not sent — a mechanic that is more favourable to us than the playbook requires. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, matching the preferred cap, requires ninety days' notice of any increase, and protects prepaid periods. The three-year initial term in § 8.1 is a negotiated committed term, not an automatic multi-year renewal, so it does not trigger the walk-away test. No redline warranted.
